# Incident Report: 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 | Source of all C2 traffic; hub of top IP conversations |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 | ARP: `172.17.0.99 -> 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4` (bidirectional, opcodes 1 and 2) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT | NBNS broadcast from 172.17.0.99: `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>` (Workstation/Redirector) and `<20>` (Server service); AD domain `bepositive.com` |
| Logged-in user | afletcher | Kerberos `CNameString` field exchanged bidirectionally between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17 |

Domain controller / DNS server for context: **172.17.0.17**, hostname `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com`, MAC `00:23:ae:50:ba:fd` — this is infrastructure, not a second victim.

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer (Win32/Koi Stealer)** — **signature-confirmed**.

The supplied Suricata alert export contains `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (Event #3.1504, 48 hits, first seen 2024-09-04 17:35 UTC), firing on `172.17.0.99 -> 79.124.78.197:80`. This is corroborated directly in the pcap: 96 `POST /foots.php` requests to 79.124.78.197 between **17:35:07 and 18:31:55 UTC** (the entire remaining capture window), each carrying a fixed pipe-delimited beacon body, e.g.:

```
101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
```

The middle field (`30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`) is a stable per-infection bot ID reused across all beacons. The server (`nginx`) replies with an empty `200 OK` each time — a live check-in loop, not one-off exfiltration. This matches the alert-named family and its known checkin structure.

## Indicators of Compromise
